Prediction (>=0.5) REFUTED. Oddity: the dataset listing (E0003) shows answers equal to the token at position 12 (the true repeat-next token), but the baseline's 'expected' strings for the same prompts (E0002: ' isoform',' readers',' speed','INSERT') differ from the strings for those listed answer ids when I pass them explicitly (E0004: ' Vo',' ess','akia',' normally'). So the targets the task scores against are not the listed/true repeat-next tokens. In E0004 (explicit prompts+targets, n=8) accuracy is 0.25; the model's prediction for example 3 (' ess') equals the expected string of example 1, which suggests explicitly supplied targets may also be permuted across examples. Need a permutation-invariant check before concluding anything about model ability.

The model can copy the repeat-next token; the baseline failures come from scored targets being decoupled (permuted across examples) from the inputs. On 8 prompts built so that every example has the SAME repeat-next token (15315 at position 12), any permutation of targets is a no-op, so accuracy should be high.

text: Permutation-invariant check (E0005, local-full, n=8, all prompts share repeat-next token 15315): accuracy 0.75 (6/8), mean logprob -1.60 clean vs -13.99 corrupt. Confirmed. Also, token 15315 decodes as 'arity' in E0005, whereas in E0004 the target I supplied at index 0 (15315) was displayed as ' Vo': the lab permutes targets across examples even when supplied explicitly. Conclusion: in this investigation the scored targets are decoupled from the inputs (shuffled across examples). Against those targets the model is at chance (E0002: 1/64, no clean/corrupt gap), so there is no input->target behaviour to explain on the task as defined. The model itself does copy the repeat-next token when the shuffle is neutralised, but that is an 8-prompt, single-answer-token observation and not a basis for a mechanism claim.

Stop after 5 experiments. Per protocol, baseline at chance on the task dataset means there is no mechanism to explain; no screening, patching or verify_hypothesis is run, because every task-level metric would be computed against targets unrelated to the inputs and any 'circuit' found would be noise. No mechanism is claimed. Report as null result with the label-decoupling diagnosis.
